title: Clarification on Withdrawal of CPF Savings at Payout Eligibility Age
what_it_is: Clarification on Withdrawal of CPF Savings at Payout Eligibility Age

sections.label: CPF payout age questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the CPF payout default age will be revised from 70 to 65 and about public communication and notification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower given the feedback and concerns received regarding the CPF payout under the Retirement Sum Scheme, whether the CPF Board will consider revising the default option for CPF payout age to 65 years instead of the current 70 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether sufficient public communication was done prior to the letters being sent to individuals with regard to the option on the timing of their CPF payout; (b) whether there are other approaches to notify the general public of this option before the official process kicks in; and (c) for those who have earlier failed to notify CPF that they wish to receive their payouts upon age 65, whether they are allowed to do so at any point of time before they turn 70.

sections.label: RSS payout activation statistics questions
sections.summary: Questions ask for numbers on RSS members activating payouts, appeals, and whether the default payout age will be set to the PEA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower since the start of 2018 (a) what is the number and proportion of members on the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS) who activated their CPF payouts upon reaching their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA); (b) what is the number of members who, having missed the activation deadline, appealed to start their payouts before age 70; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider setting the default automatic CPF payout age of RSS and CPF Life scheme to the PEA to further simplify the activation process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) for each year of age between 65 and 70 what is the proportion of eligible CPF members who apply to start payouts; (b) for members of the 65 to 70 age group receiving payouts, what is known about their use of payout monies, in particular, the extent to which payouts are retained in low-interest deposit accounts instead of used for expenses; and (c) whether and to what extent there are cases of financial hardship due to eligible members not applying to receive payouts.

sections.label: Payout Eligibility Age remains 65
sections.summary: From 1 January 2018 the PEA has been 65, and it has not shifted to 70.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From 1 January 2018, the PEA has been 65.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have not shifted the PEA from 65 to 70, as was alleged by a spurious online post.

sections.label: Latest Payout Start Age of 70
sections.summary: A Latest Payout Start Age of 70 was introduced for members turning 70 from 2018, as some RSS savings stayed intact until death.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the past, some RSS members had their savings intact in their CPF accounts until they passed away.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We therefore introduced a Latest Payout Start Age of 70 for members turning 70 from 2018.

sections.label: Interest from deferring payouts
sections.summary: Deferring payouts earns CPF savings risk-free interest of up to 6% yearly, and CPF LIFE payouts rise up to 7% per year deferred.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With every year that they defer their payouts, their CPF savings will earn risk-free interest of up to 6% a year, which is well above the interest rates they would get in the market.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For members on CPF LIFE, for every year deferred, the payouts go up by up to 7%.

sections.label: RSS members not starting payouts
sections.summary: At the end of 2017, six in 10 RSS members who reached their PEA that year did not start payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the end of 2017, six in 10 members on the RSS who had reached their PEA that year did not start their payouts.

sections.label: SSO staff ask about CPF payouts
sections.summary: SSO staff will ask members seeking financial help whether they have activated CPF payouts and help them do so if they wish.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, where appropriate, staff at the Social Service Offices (SSOs) will ask members who approach the SSOs for financial help whether they have activated their CPF payouts and assist them to do so if they wish.

sections.label: CPF payout start timing
sections.summary: About 35,000 members received payouts at their PEA by end-2018, and members can start payouts between PEA and 70 by instructing CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, by the end of 2018, about 35,000 of such members had already started to receive their payouts upon reaching their PEA, which is what they expected.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members who joined CPF LIFE after July 2015 will be like members on the RSS.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They can start their payouts any time between their PEA and 70, by instructing CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All members can start their payouts any time after PEA by issuing a simple instruction to CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, the exact payout application process and letters sent to members may vary, depending on each member’s particular circumstances, such as whether they are on RSS or when they joined CPF LIFE.

sections.label: Members not withdrawing CPF
sections.summary: About 60% of CPF members do not withdraw at 65, and about half do not come forward even at 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I think this is very important and very re-assuring for CPF members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But I am concerned that about 60% of CPF members do not come forward to withdraw their CPF when they reach 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Minister said that about half of CPF members do not come forward to withdraw their CPF even when they have reached 70 years of age.

sections.label: Automatic payout at 65 question
sections.summary: The speaker asks why payouts cannot be made automatic at age 65 if CPF Board can do so at 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If CPF Board can do so at age 70, why not make the payout automatic at the age of 65?

sections.label: Employment rate ages 65 to 69
sections.summary: Between ages 65 and 69, the employment rate today is about 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: After all, between the age of 65 and 69 today, our employment rate is about 40%.

sections.label: Review of CPF letter
sections.summary: The Minister said CPF Board will review the letter sent to members at age 65, including the statement that no action is required to start payouts at 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Minister said that the CPF Board will review the letter that is sent to members when the members reach age 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope that the CPF Board can review this particular statement that is made in the letter, "No action is required if you wish to start your payout at age of 70".

sections.label: CPF Board letter types
sections.summary: The CPF Board sends out about 220 types of letters in total.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you put together all the letters that CPF Board sends out, there are about 220 types.

sections.label: Invitation at PEA 65
sections.summary: From this year, members reaching their PEA of 65 will be invited again for face-to-face personalised guidance from the CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From this year onwards, once they reach their PEA, which is 65, we will equally invite the member to come again, so that CPF Board can provide personalised guidance, face-to-face.

sections.label: Reminder for unactivated payouts
sections.summary: CPF records will show if a member reached the PEA without activating payouts, and the Board will remind them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: CPF records will show whether the member has reached the PEA but has not activated payouts, in which case CPF Board will remind the individual that "You have reached the PEA.

sections.label: Identifying aware non-starters
sections.summary: Establishing which members are aware and consciously chose not to start payouts would be a major exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: CPF Board must be quite mindful that not everyone wants to tell the Board the reasons for their actions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, if we want to establish, amongst those who have not started their payouts, who actually is aware and made a conscious decision not to start it, who is not aware and did not come forward to instruct the Board, this would be quite a major exercise.

sections.label: Use of earlier PEA payouts
sections.summary: The question asks what is known about whether payouts at earlier PEAs are used for expenses or sit in near-zero savings accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The last question is, what is known right now about the use of payouts at the earlier PEAs, that is, are the payouts used for expenses or do they sit largely in zero percent or close to zero percent savings accounts?

sections.label: Re-employment age raised to 67
sections.summary: The re-employment age was first 65, raised to 67 in July 2017, and both retirement and re-employment ages are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the Singapore context, the re-employment age, when it was first implemented, was to age 65.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Then, in July 2017, we raised the re-employment age to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, in fact, Singaporeans have the assurance of employment beyond the retirement age of 62, all the way up to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In any case, both the retirement age and the re-employment age are being reviewed.

sections.label: CPF withdrawals placed in bank accounts
sections.summary: A survey suggests slightly over half of members put their CPF withdrawals at age 55 into a bank account earning poorer interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our survey suggests that slightly over half of the members, after taking the withdrawals from their CPF accounts at the age of 55, just put it in a bank account, earning much poorer interest rates.

sections.label: Member complaint on payout tenure
sections.summary: A CPF member complained that CPF Board would stretch his payouts over 28 years until age 93 instead of 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A CPF member had complained that CPF Board would stretch his payouts over 28 years until he is 93, when he thought it should be 20 years, on the assumption if the tenure was shorter, he would get more over these 20 years.

sections.label: Singapore residents living beyond 85
sections.summary: In 2017, more than half of Singapore residents aged 65 were expected to live beyond 85, and one in five to about 95 or above.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2017, more than half, one in two Singapore residents aged 65 was expected to live beyond 85.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: One in five of them was expected to live to about 95 or above.

sections.label: CPF LIFE and RSS coverage
sections.summary: CPF LIFE provides lifelong payouts but is mandatory only for those turning 65 in 2023 with $60,000 in their Retirement Account, so most elderly remain on the RSS.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The better solution for the member to managing this longevity risk is CPF LIFE, which provides lifelong payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, because CPF LIFE is mandatory only for those turning age 65 in 2023, with $60,000 in Retirement Account balance, most of our elderly will still not be on CPF LIFE but remain on the RSS.

sections.label: RSS members taking up CPF LIFE
sections.summary: About 92,500 RSS members have taken up CPF LIFE voluntarily.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, I am happy to share with the Member that about 92,500 RSS members have taken up CPF LIFE voluntarily.

sections.label: Reminders on payout start age
sections.summary: Members who did not want to start payouts at PEA are reminded year after year through the Yearly Statement of Account until age 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: For members who did not want to start their payout at PEA, will they be reminded again every year until age 70?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They are reminded year after year, through the Yearly Statement of Account.

sections.label: CPF payouts without LPA
sections.summary: If no instruction is received by 70, the CPF Board will stream out payments, and without an LPA it is hard to see how payouts could start before 70.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If by 70, there has been no instruction received, the CPF Board will also stream out the payments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If he does not have the LPA, it would be very hard to see how the CPF Board could be instructed to start the payouts even before 70.

sections.label: Number coming on-board
sections.summary: Quite a number have decided to come on-board, and they are part of the 92,500 shared.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Quite a number have decided that they will come on-board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They are part of the 92,500 that I shared.
